extractor_notes: Two granted classes, matching INDEX.md. The 2000 codified text in § 201.40(b) is unusually terse: each class is a single descriptive noun phrase with no separately enumerated permitted uses, exclusions, or definitions. The general framing in § 201.40(a) (and the (b) chapeau) merely restates that the § 1201(a)(1)(A) prohibition does not apply to users of the listed classes. No conditions, qualifying users, definitions of 'obsoleteness', or limits on permitted uses are codified at the regulation level in this cycle. The decomposition below pulls the implicit 'permitted use' (i.e., circumvention of the relevant access control) from the (b) chapeau and the (a) general clause, and treats the descriptive qualifiers in each class as definitions/conditions. Sub-paragraph (a) is on PDF p. 19 along with sub-paragraph (b); the full codified § 201.40 is contained on a single PDF page.

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Compilations consisting of lists of websites blocked by filtering software applications
permitted_uses: Circumvention of technological measures that effectively control access to compilations consisting of lists of websites blocked by filtering software applications, by users of such compilations, for noninfringing uses
exclusions: Exemption is effective only for the period from October 28, 2000 to October 28, 2003
definitions_or_conditions: The class is limited to compilations 'consisting of lists of websites blocked by filtering software applications' — i.e., the block-lists themselves, not the filtering software
Available only to 'users of' the prescribed class of copyrighted works whose noninfringing uses are, or are likely to be, adversely affected (§ 201.40(a))

source.quote: § 201.40 Exemption to prohibition against circumvention. (a) General. This section prescribes the classes of copyrighted works for which the Librarian of Congress has determined, pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 1201(a)(1)(C) and (D), that noninfringing uses by persons who are users of such works are, or are likely to be, adversely affected. The prohibition against circumvention of technological measures that control access to copyrighted works set forth in 17 U.S.C. 1201(a)(1)(A) shall not apply to such users of the prescribed classes of copyrighted works. (b) Classes of copyrighted works. Pursuant to the authority set forth in 17 U.S.C. 1201(a)(1)(C) and (D), and upon the recommendation of the Register of copyrights, the Librarian has determined that two classes of copyrighted works shall be subject to the exemption found in 17 U.S.C. 1201(a)(1)(B) from the prohibition against circumvention of technological measures that effectively control access to copyrighted works set forth in 17 U.S.C. 1201(a)(1)A) for the period from October 28, 2000 to October 28, 2003. The exempted classes of works are: (1) Compilations consisting of lists of websites blocked by filtering software applications; and

exemptions.equipment_or_work: Literary works, including computer programs and databases, protected by access control mechanisms that fail to permit access because of malfunction, damage or obsoleteness
permitted_uses: Circumvention of technological measures that effectively control access to literary works (including computer programs and databases) whose access control mechanisms fail to permit access, by users of such works, for noninfringing uses
exclusions: Limited to literary works whose access control mechanism 'fail[s] to permit access' — i.e., the exemption does not reach functioning access controls
The failure must be 'because of malfunction, damage or obsoleteness'; other reasons for inaccessibility are not covered
Exemption is effective only for the period from October 28, 2000 to October 28, 2003
definitions_or_conditions: The class of works is defined as 'Literary works, including computer programs and databases' — the parenthetical confirms that computer programs and databases qualifying as literary works are within scope
The triggering condition is access-control failure attributable to 'malfunction, damage or obsoleteness' (the codified text does not further define these terms)
Available only to 'users of' the prescribed class of copyrighted works whose noninfringing uses are, or are likely to be, adversely affected (§ 201.40(a))
